name: Toby Keith
notes: Barroom-anthem country — loud, chant-hook, rock-guitar-forward. The kit is authored from the entry's own claim that "his producer was himself a career session drummer, and the records show it — the groove is the arrangement's spine and fills are placed only at 4- and 8-bar boundaries": quarter-note kick under choruses (four-on-the-floor-adjacent), 8th hats, crash accents on chorus downbeats, and a fill grid pinned to 4/8. Harmony is the stated "I–IV–V and I–♭VII–IV–I for the rock cuts," plus the anthem device the entry names outright — "the anthems park on a I–V two-chord vamp for whole verses," which is why a two-chord family and a `vamp`-weighted harmonic rhythm are authored. The melody is chant-shaped as described: "repeated-note verses in a narrow fourth or fifth, chorus built on a single rhythmic cell repeated," so the register is narrow, the interval mix is step-heavy and `twoBarCellRepeat` is high. ⚠ Confidence is medium (research: high-medium) and the per-track key/tempo readings are marked [LOW-CONF] there. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are the velocity tiers, the cell-repeat value and the countermelody ratio — "rock-sized backbeat," "note density low" and "steel used as colour rather than lead" are directions, and 108–127, 0.55 and 0.36 are this author's reading of them. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 978/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor), and every other lever this gate has was already clean here** — no empty-bar bias, no one-bar phrase length, and no lead allowed to thin below two notes a bar.
